title: Peak hip, knee and ankle joint moments across common sports movements
subtitle: Scoping evidence snapshot, not a validated normative dataset
generated_by: literature scan compiled for bioscout_web; see review_joint_moment_norms.md for the narrative and caveats

how_to_read.units: Nm/kg unless noted otherwise. Some sources normalise to Nm/(kg*m) (body mass x height) instead of Nm/kg — these are flagged explicitly and must NOT be compared directly to Nm/kg values.
how_to_read.confidence: point_estimate = a specific mean(+-SD) peak moment reported for a defined sample/condition. direction_only = the source supports a trend (X rises with Y) but no single defensible peak value was extracted. none = searched, no usable value found.
how_to_read.tier: Reuses the A/B/C tiers from ../2026_Sep_MiniReview_MSK_modelling_sporting_tasks/studies.json and adds tier D for this review. B = reportable with an explicit uncertainty band, population-level only. D = no defensible population norm exists yet — do not publish a number, even with caveats.
how_to_read.warning: Every value below is contingent on load, speed, sport, sex and/or measurement method in ways that make it unsafe to present as a general 'normal range' without the attached sample/condition. Do not strip a value from its condition field.

findings.note: increases with running speed (8 -> 12 -> 16 km/h); ankle plantarflexor moment increases proportionally more than knee extensor moment across the same speed range
correlates with sprint acceleration magnitude (R^2=0.47); knee extensor moment impulse does not correlate with acceleration
findings.source: Colyer, Nagahara & Salo 2019, Journal of Experimental Biology
